sentences.text: Case of the prosecution is that, on the complaint filed by one Mohankumar on 27.05.2024, the police have registered the NC: 2024:KHC-K:9603 case.

It is stated that the complainant came in contact with accused Nos.1 to 6 and they assured the complainant that, if the complainant invest `4,00,000/- within one year, they will give double the money and they are running the Company in the name of 'Capital Grow Learn Trading' and they have convinced the complainant to invest `4,00,000/- and the bond has also been executed.
Since the accused did not pay the money from the Company, a complaint came to be lodged.

During investigation, it came to the knowledge of the Sri Utkarsh Vardhamane vs State Of Karnataka on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75437349/
3 police that the petitioners have cheated various people, that too, more than 30 crores as per the submissions of learned HCGP.

sentences.text: Now the investigation is in progress and the police are trying to arrest these petitioners.
Hence, they are before this Court for grant of anticipatory bail.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioners contended that there were four cases registered by the police against these petitioners in Crime Nos.33, 34, 36 and 37/2024.
The petitioners have been arrested by the police in connection with Crime No.33/3024 and they have been interrogated by the Investigating Officer.
However, the charge sheet was not filed within 90 days.
Therefore, they have been released on NC: 2024:KHC-K:9603 statutory bail under Section 167(2) of Cr.P.C.

After release,
they also moved the bail application before the Sessions Judge in Crime Nos.34/2024 and 37/2024,
where they have been granted anticipatory bail.
However, anticipatory bail in Crime No.36/2024 has been rejected.
Hence, they are before this Court.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioners contended that there is nothing to recover from the petitioners during the custodial interrogation for more than 90 days.
The police have not filed the charge sheet.
There is nothing on record to show the involvement of the petitioners.
They are ready to abide by any of the conditions that would be imposed by this Court.
6. Learned HCGP., objected to the bail petitions and contended that they have cheated more than a sum of `30 crores.
7. Upon hearing the learned HCGP, ofcourse, the petitioners have approached the Sessions Judge for grant of anticipatory bail, which came to be rejected.

However, it is not in dispute that these accused persons were already arrested by the very same police in Crime No.33/2024 and the accused persons NC: 2024:KHC-K:9603 were in custody for more than 90 days.

The police have not able to file the charge sheet, therefore, they have been granted a statutory bail under Section 167(2)
of Cr.P.C. and after the release, in other three cases, they have moved the anticipatory bail application.
Out of which, in two cases they were granted anticipatory bail by the learned Sessions Judge and one bail petition is rejected.
8. The allegations against all the accused persons in connection with Crime No.36/2024 is that, they have cheated 4 lakhs to the complainant.
One of the accused is already granted anticipatory bail by this Court.
The learned Sessions Judge granted bail to the same accused person in other two cases and the accused persons were already in custody and undergone interrogation in Crime No.33/2024.

When such being the case, the petitioners are not required for custodial interrogation in order to reject the anticipatory bail and the offences are not punishable either with death or imprisonment for life.

The apprehension expressed by the learned HCGP that if the petitioners are granted anticipatory bail, they may no co- operate with the investigation or that they may tamper the NC: 2024:KHC-K:9603 prosecution witnesses, can be safeguarded by imposing stringent conditions.
